html:
The Takelma are a Native American people who lived in the Rogue Valley of southwest Oregon. Most of their villages stood along the Rogue River. They spoke the Takelma language, which has no close relatives.

They fished for salmon, gathered acorns and camas, and hunted deer. Their neighbours included the Tututni downriver and the Shasta to the south.

Gold was found near Jacksonville in 1851, and miners and settlers poured in. Clashes grew into the Rogue River Wars of 1855 and 1856. Afterwards the Takelma were marched and shipped north to reservations, and their descendants belong to the Siletz and Grand Ronde tribes. In 1906 the linguist Edward Sapir recorded their language from Frances Johnson, one of the last speakers.
